name: BrightstarDB
tagline: MIT-licensed RDF triple store for .NET with SPARQL and a LINQ-based entity framework; dormant since 2020.
description: BrightstarDB is a native RDF triple store written in C# for the .NET platform that runs either embedded in your process or as a server exposing a SPARQL 1.1 endpoint and REST API. Its distinguishing feature was a code-first entity framework: you declare .NET interfaces, BrightstarDB generates classes that persist as RDF, and a LINQ provider translates queries into SPARQL, so you get ORM-style development over a schema-free graph. It started as a commercial product from NetworkedPlanet and went open source under MIT in 2013. The last stable release was 1.13.3.1 in February 2018, a 1.14 alpha followed in 2019, and the repository has seen only a dependency bump since 2020. Existing .NET apps can keep running it, but new RDF projects are better served by a maintained store such as GraphDB, Stardog, Oxigraph or Jena.
statusNote: Dormant: last stable release 1.13.3.1 (Feb 2018), a 1.14 alpha in 2019, and only a dependency update since 2020.

pricing.notes: Free under MIT; NetworkedPlanet historically offered commercial support.

scale.notes: Single-node store sized for application-level graphs rather than large knowledge graphs.

strengths: Code-first entity framework maps .NET interfaces to RDF and translates LINQ queries to SPARQL
Runs embedded in-process with zero configuration or as a standalone SPARQL 1.1 server
Schema-free RDF model makes merging differently shaped data straightforward
Its LINQ-to-SPARQL layer can also target other SPARQL 1.1 endpoints
weaknesses: No stable release since 2018 and no meaningful development since 2020
Tied to .NET; little tooling or community outside that ecosystem
Single-node only, with no clustering or replication
Small user base, so issues often go unanswered
useCases: Maintaining existing .NET apps built on its entity framework
Embedded RDF storage inside desktop or mobile .NET apps
Studying a LINQ-to-SPARQL object mapping layer
